summary.intent: Work through a series of audit-fix clusters in the callisto repo, each on its own branch with a PR, pushing branches and delegating fixes to subagents. This stretch covered finishing cluster 5a and cluster 5b (the dual-manifest cascade source bug).
summary.outcome: Cluster 5a was pushed, and six branches are now waiting for PRs. The cluster 5b subagent reproduced and fixed the dual-manifest cascade bug in `derive_release_decision`, with a new graph test, a spec update and a changeset. The fix was committed signed, and cluster 6 (missing tests) is next.

repo: `callisto version --emit-decision` failed with a ReleaseInvariant error when a bumped dependent's source package had two canonical manifests (e.g. Cargo and npm), because it looked up a single release id.

Rule adopted per ADR 0012 and docs/architecture/release.md: a dependent waits only for the dependency's distribution in its own ecosystem. `from` is the source distribution the dependent's dependency edge points at.
Edges are matched by `to == via`, the same dep kind (`Peer` for escalations) and the same rendered spec. The edge's ecosystem comes from `crate::cascade::manifest_ecosystem(edge.from_manifest)`.
`derive_selected_release_decision` goes through `derive_release_decision`, so the fix covers it. No other code maps `via` to a release id.
The sandbox blocks network and the uv cache, so `native_resolution_e2e_tests::pnpm_and_uv_workspace_resolves_natively_after_version` fails there; it is unrelated to the fix.
Changesets are created with `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:patch --summary ...`.
Work happens in the git worktree `.claude/worktrees/audit-fixes`, with one branch per audit cluster.

code.finding: New `cascade_source` helper. `reason_from_bump` now takes the graph, the dependent and the entry's release id, and both the Cascade and PeerEscalation branches use the helper. A single-release-id source short-circuits, so existing behaviour is unchanged. ReleaseInvariant remains only for no matching edge or for several candidate distributions with none in the entry's ecosystem.

New test `release_decision_names_the_dual_source_distribution_each_dependent_uses` builds an inline workspace with cargo, npm, peer and dual-manifest dependents of a Cargo+npm package. Lines 218 and 222 hold pre-existing over-120-column string literals.
VER-APPLY-10 now describes the cascade `from` field as the source distribution the dependent's dependency names, the one in the entry's own ecosystem when it names several.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user instructions. The report's claims should be checked, for example by re-running the tests, before relying on them.
Subagents were told to skip `just ci` and network-dependent tests, so the parent session needs to run broader verification itself.
Each cluster gets its own branch and PR body file, pushed and committed signed.

friction: The peer-escalation failure could not be reproduced on its own because the decision stops at the first error.
One callisto-cli e2e test fails in the sandbox because pnpm cannot reach registry.npmjs.org and the uv cache is not permitted.
Clippy flagged an `or_else` that had to be changed to `or`, which forced a second test run.
open_items: Open PRs for the six pushed branches, plus the cluster 5b branch once it is pushed.
Cluster 6 (missing tests) is still to do.
Run `just ci` and the network-dependent e2e test outside the sandbox, since the subagent skipped them.
No CLI-level test was added for the emit-decision fix; it relies on the graph test and a manual binary run.
A dependent with three or more manifests whose dependencies match none of the candidate distributions still ends in ReleaseInvariant.
